:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Calculating the Determinant of a 2x2 Matrix With Integer Entries

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
For a $2 \times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}|
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & -2 \\ 0 & \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}| \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{3}-(-2)\cdot 0 \\  & =\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Calculating the Determinant of a 2x2 Matrix With Non-Integer Entries

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
If
${A} = 
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        2 & -1 \
        -3 & k
    }
    \right\rbrack$
and
$\det({A}) = 5$, what is the value of $k?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
For a $2 \times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}|
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -3 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot k-(-1)\cdot (-3) \\  & =2k-3\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\det(A)=5,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =5 \\ 2k-3 & =5 \\ 2k & =8 \\ k & =4\end{aligned}
$$
